one-line thesis: Vidya Wires achieved 24.2% revenue growth and margin expansion in FY26 by successfully commissioning its ALCU subsidiary, which introduced high-margin specialized products for EV and renewables; the company now enters FY27 with 36,000 MT capacity and a clear path to margin uplift through product mix shift, making it a structural beneficiary of India’s grid and energy transition capex.
financial scorecard: revenue: +24.2% YoY; EBITDA: +35 bps margin to 4.66%; PAT: ₹576.1M (rptd); order book: not disclosed; net debt: reduced by ₹100Cr via IPO proceeds repayment; one-offs: ALCU ramp-up costs not fully absorbed in FY26, no accounting distortions noted
guidance: revenue growth: strong volume growth expected; margin: improvement expected from higher-value product mix; order inflow: aligned with ALCU capacity ramp-up; capex/commissioning: full 36,000 MT capacity by Diwali FY26, no further capex announced
segment / subsidiary detail: Power & transmission: 51%; Renewable & EV: 7%; General engineering: 13%; Electricals: 27%; Consumer durables: 3%
growth verticals / optionality: ALCU facility enables entry into PV round ribbon, CTC, copper foils, and aluminium conductors; export target of 25% (currently 12%); land available for future capacity expansion
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved 35 bps to 4.66% due to back-to-back hedging; new products (aluminium, CTC, PV ribbon) carry higher EBITDA/ton than traditional copper wires; aluminum processing adds 3.5x value-add vs copper
capex / expansion: ₹100Cr of IPO proceeds used for ALCU capex; total capacity expanded from ~19,000 MT to 36,000 MT; no further capex announced beyond FY26
capital allocation: IPO proceeds prioritized: 1) ALCU capex, 2) ₹100Cr debt repayment; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on organic growth and balance sheet strength
risks & watch-items: logistical delays from Middle East conflict; ocean freight inflation; raw material price volatility (mitigated by hedging); competitive capacity expansion by Precision Wires, Ram Ratna, KSH
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, and disciplined; emphasized phased ramp-up, margin protection, and long-term value creation; avoided giving hard FY27 guidance but signaled strong volume and margin upside
non-obvious takeaways: GST subsidy of 45-50% of ALCU investment over 10 years from Gujarat govt; CTC product launch delayed to Oct FY26; copper foil targeting transformers/switchgear, not semiconductors; 35-40% plant fungibility allows dynamic product mix shift

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration for quality control and sustainability: primary raw material is copper rods made from copper cathodes; the Company has backward-integrated its manufacturing facility to produce oxygen-free copper rods from copper cathodes in-house. About 35%-40% of total copper rod requirement was manufactured in-house from copper cathodes during the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and the last 3 Fiscals, with the remainder purchased from suppliers. Raw material requirements are met through a mix of imports and local procurement; imports constituted about 30%-56% of total raw material requirements during the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and the last 3 Fiscals. Major raw material suppliers include Vedanta Limited, Marubeni Corporation, Union Copper Rod LLC, Hindalco Industries Ltd., Bharat Aluminium Company Ltd. and Ducab Metals LLC, with over ten years of relationship maintained with Vedanta Limited, Union Copper Rod LLC and Hindalco Industries Ltd.

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (pre-approved supplier status)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Capacity utilisation improved from 70.31% in Fiscal 2023 to 94.51% in the three months ended June 30, 2025, indicating operating leverage as volumes scale
- High proportion of revenue from repeat customers (94.28% in FY25, 88.90% in FY24, 82.96% in FY23) supports revenue visibility
- Copper rod/cathode constitutes the dominant share of raw material purchases (93.87% in FY25, 96.51% in FY24, 96.19% in FY23), exposing costs and margins to copper price movements
- Revenue mix increasingly weighted to the Power & transmission segment (48.06% of FY25 revenue vs 46.37% in FY23)
- Revenue concentration in Gujarat and Maharashtra (68.66%-69.88% of revenue from operations across the periods presented)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand manufacturing capabilities and further diversify product range to enhance market position
- Continue to integrate environmental, social and governance practices into business with a sustainable and responsible approach to operations
- Add new products through the Proposed Project — Copper Foils, Copper Components, Continuously Transposed Copper Conductors, PV Round Ribbon, Solar Cables, Multi Paper Covered Copper Conductors, Enameled Aluminium Winding Wires, and Enameled Aluminium Rectangular Strips

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company proposes to increase installed capacity from 19,680 MT per annum to 37,680 MT per annum by installing additional 18,000 MTPA at a new manufacturing unit ("Proposed Project") at Narsanda, Taluka Nadiad, Gujarat, 15 kms from its existing operating facilities, under wholly owned subsidiary ALCU Industries Private Limited. Through the Proposed Project, the Company intends to add new products including Copper Foils, Copper Components, Continuously Transposed Copper Conductors, PV Round Ribbon, Solar Cables, Multi Paper Covered Copper Conductors, Enameled Aluminium Winding Wires, and Enameled Aluminium Rectangular Strips. Post-expansion, market share of installed capacity is expected to rise from 5.7% (FY25) to 11.0%, and the Company expects to move from 4th to 3rd largest manufacturer in India by installed capacity, ceteris paribus.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Among the top 5 manufacturers in the winding and conductivity products industry in India (4th largest by installed capacity; 5.7% market share of installed capacity in FY25)
- De-risked business model with wide customer base, diversified portfolio of products and multiple end-user industries (over 318 customers, none contributing over 9% of annual revenue; over 8,000 SKUs)
- Backward integration for quality control as well as sustainability initiatives
- Presence in a strategically located region (Anand, Gujarat, with logistics access to major seaports)
- Diversified customer base with longstanding relationships with customers and suppliers (over ten years with major suppliers such as Vedanta Limited, Union Copper Rod LLC and Hindalco Industries Ltd)
- Continuous financial performance
- Experienced professional management team

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Revenue concentration in power & transmission, general engineering and electrical sectors — Over 80% of revenue from operations (81.09% in Q1 FY26, 87.13% in FY25, 87.33% in FY24, 89.54% in FY23) was derived from these three sectors; any slowdown in these sectors may impact the business
- Raw material price volatility and supply dependency (copper, aluminium, insulation material) — Copper Rod/Cathode alone constituted 93.87% of raw material purchases in FY25 (96.51% in FY24); price fluctuations, shortages or supply disruptions could materially affect costs, sales and timelines
- Geographic revenue concentration in Gujarat and Maharashtra — These two states constituted 68.66%-69.88% of revenue from operations across the three months ended June 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2023-2025
- Reliance on a commissioned industry report (CareEdge Report) for industry/market data — Industry and market data used throughout the DRHP is derived from a report exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company; the DRHP itself flags that reliance on such information for investment decisions carries inherent risk
- Differences between Ind AS and other accounting principles (US GAAP/IFRS) — Audited financial statements are prepared under Indian Accounting Standards, which differ materially from US GAAP and IFRS, flagged as a risk factor for investors more familiar with those standards
